display.purpose: Large menu title; prepared bold bitmap face.

body.purpose: HUD counters, Russian descriptions, values, and hints.

motion.name: selection-swap
motion.purpose: Immediate native texture or bottom-strip swap; no animated focus transition.

motion.name: heart-blink
motion.purpose: Invulnerability blink cycle, using the original full/half blinking sprite for the first 0.1 s. Runs only with flashes enabled and reads world.clock.

motion.name: chapter-one-ending
motion.purpose: Simulation-clock sequence beginning at 12:00: arrival 0–4 s, storm 4–13 s, inferno 13–24 s, collapse 24–26 s, portal 26–29 s, fall 29–34 s. Pause and character stats freeze this clock.

motion.name: chapter-music-crossfade
motion.purpose: Separate normal and supplied Herobrine OGG players crossfade on arrival; menu and retry restore normal music. Uses audio process time and continues during simulation pauses.

nativeRenderer.previewTranslation: Inline SVG paths retain pixels from the actual local GUI sprites and bitmap glyph atlases. These static browser documentation previews are not runtime components; buttons and the upgrade choice additionally expose the observed selected state on hover/focus. Tonal ramps are documentation exploration metadata, not new runtime colors.

components.name: Native health row
components.description: Ten original 9 × 9 heart containers on an 8 px stride; static example is 16 / 20 HP. In-game invulnerability blinking uses simulation time and the flashes setting.

components.name: Experience track and level
components.description: Original experience textures at the actual 256 × 5 HUD size with a separate level label. Example: level 17, 3 / 53 XP, yielding a 14 px fill.

components.name: Six-slot weapon bar
components.description: The 122 × 22 hotbar-derived texture, native sword, level label, and original selected-slot frame. The frame extends one pixel beyond the bar at the top and left. Inventory display only.

components.name: Black character sheet — attribute excerpt
components.description: Exact coordinate excerpt of the left attribute column (viewport x = 0–282, y = 120–272) on opaque black. Values are the real level-one baseline with no passives. Full sheet behavior and equipment regions are specified in DESIGN.md.

narrative.overview:
This document captures the HUD, typography, shared controls, character sheet, and scoped Chapter I extension (0.5) in the existing native Godot game. The visual authority is the user's requested Minecraft appearance and the local Minecraft Java 1.21.11 textures, GUI sprites, and bitmap providers. It records the shipped implementation, rather than establishing a separate product identity.

Dense pixel information uses white and gray text over charcoal or black. Native hearts, experience, and item art carry their existing color meanings. The character sheet is an opaque black interruption of the arena, with live attributes, equipment, and a direct return to the prior game state.

The start menu contains only “Minecraft Survivors” and three functional buttons. Actors now use vanilla texture UVs on animated cuboids baked into the existing 2D atlas format. Chapter I extends this same world with Herobrine's throne, a burning arena, and a Nether teaser; its dramatic color belongs to the scene rather than the shared interface.
keyCharacteristics: Original Minecraft bitmap glyphs, including Russian text.
Gray beveled controls and square monochrome frames.
Native heart, experience, and hotbar-derived equipment sprites.
A fixed logical viewport with integer scaling and nearest sampling.
An opaque black character sheet that preserves the interrupted state.
Vanilla-textured cuboid actors and a deterministic, unavoidable Chapter I ending.

rules.name: The Semantic Color Rule
rules.body: Keep interface chrome neutral. Preserve the original color of health, experience, and item art instead of adding decorative accents to controls or panels.

rules.name: The Whole Pixel Rule
rules.body: Preserve bitmap glyphs and whole base-size multiples. The black shadow offset is one logical pixel per 8 px of text size; use nearest sampling throughout.

dos: **Do** reuse the original GUI sprites and prepared Minecraft bitmap fonts.
**Do** keep all layout coordinates in the 640 × 360 logical viewport and preserve integer scaling.
**Do** use white and gray for interface chrome while retaining semantic health, experience, and item colors.
**Do** derive displayed attributes and weapon values from the same data and formulas as combat.
**Do** preserve the exact interrupted state and frozen run time when opening and closing character stats.
**Do** preserve the complete seated Herobrine silhouette and use only branchless vertical trunks for the scorched trees.
donts: **Don't** replace native hearts or bitmap text with emoji, vector approximations, or smoothed substitute fonts in the game.
**Don't** introduce colorful panel themes, rounded cards, gradients, or soft interface shadows into this scoped system.
**Don't** treat legacy `GOLD`, `LIME`, or panel color arguments as permission to restore colored interface chrome.
**Don't** stretch the viewport or font glyphs by fractional display factors.
**Don't** hard-code example stats or advance the simulation while the character sheet is open.
**Don't** mix historical imagegen actor anchors into the current vanilla-textured atlas pipeline.
